utterances.text: Yes, I have it in front of me. I do apologise. I don't know if I have to state this for the record or not. I have a report here that is full of my notes. This was the report that I used while I worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm sure it will be all right, just so long as you answer my question and don't go too far beyond it. There was a revision of the number of dead and missing persons made in 2005 by Dr. Brunborg; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This revision included the inclusion of new persons, 186 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, we can see table 4, as it were, how the total numbers and the categories of them have been amended, and we see at the top -- well, if we see in the "Pros," it says the number of additional missing persons on the 2005 OTP list is about 400, i.e., 397. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if we add 397 to 7.264, I think we get 7.661, don't we?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If we go to the very top of that particular table and we add 397 to 4.969, we get 5.266. So all of the apparently additional missing persons have been added in to the category "Still Missing," haven't they?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If we look at the closed cases, dead people, that number has increased, hasn't it, from 1.979 to 2.054?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I know it's a comment you made in your report. Shouldn't the people who've since been discovered to be dead have been subtracted from those who are still missing?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have a mass, a statistical mass, where you have two elements, and you treat one of the elements as "missing," according to the characteristics, and the other element is "the dead," this very same statistical mass, if you increase one element, you don't have to be a statistician, it's only logical for the other element decrease, whereas here you have the opposite occurring. Both the number of persons ascertained dead is increased, as is the number of the people in the category of missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm fine. 5.266 minus 4.969 is 297, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's my mistake, then. Dr. Radovanovic, thank you very much. I've got no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I have to intervene here, because there is a little bit of confusion here. In table 4, for the year 2000, we have 7.264 people as the total. Dr. Brunborg, for that year, has the finding of 7.457. So if you look at the first report, the one from the year 2000, you can see that the number -- and here there is this confusion, because he takes in the data from the ICRC, and there is not full compatibility. That is why you can have a slight variation or deviation if you compared the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. And thank you, Mr. Haynes. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll not cross-examine Dr. Radovanovic, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Thank you. I do have some cross-examination for Madam Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Dr. Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We've met before, but just for the record let me state my name is Aleksandar Lazarevic, and together with my colleagues, I represent Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin before this Tribunal, and I will be cross-examining you now. So unlike my colleagues, the first three colleagues, they conducted the examination-in-chief because you were their expert, and I will be cross-examining you. The day before yesterday, we had a brief meeting, about half an hour, if you'll recall, and on that occasion I showed you some documents that I would like us to go through today in the course of your cross-examination. But apart from these documents, I will be showing you some other documents that you have not had an opportunity to go through because we didn't have much time, so now I'm going to ask you for your patience and forbearance when we get to this point when we'll have to discuss the documents that you haven't seen before. Could we please have in e-court document 3159A, but I would like this document not to be broadcast. It's already admitted into evidence, but under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Madam Registrar, you will take care of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like us to look at page 1 of this document. That's the document entitled "The Srebrenica Missing." That was the report for the year 2007, and the identification by the ICMP. It was last updated on the 11th of January, 2008. You had an opportunity to look at this document?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the cross-examination, we will be going back to this document often, and I also wanted to stress that I showed you this document in the course of this brief meeting. Could you please confirm that for the record, that this was an opportunity for you to look at this document?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask the usher's assistance, because I think it would be best to provide this document and other documents in hard copy to Professor Radovanovic. That would be the most efficient way to proceed. It would save us quite a lot of time, I think. And if my colleagues from the Prosecution want to look at it just to make sure that these are the documents that they have already received notice would be used in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, I beg your pardon, but because we are now going to mention some names, perhaps it would be best to go into private session, because I don't want any of that to be made public. This document has been used before, and every time we used it, we went into private session, so I think, out of an abundance of caution, we should do that too, again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have to adjourn because our time is up. We are continue tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. Ms. Fauveau, will you be cross-examining this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I won't, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Krgovic or Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Certainly not, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. And you, Ms. Soljan, how long do you think you will --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll try to whittle it down to under two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, so we can finish the witness tomorrow. Okay. We'll stand adjourned until 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
